title: Cut 0.9.0: the 0.8.0 section swallowed post-freeze work and carries a falsified lore claim
description:
The v0.8.0 tag is at 9d91fc35 and dev is 15 commits past it at ae9305e. Those commits include one feat (QCLI-336) and four consumer-observable fixes (QCLI-339, QCLI-340, QCLI-342, QCLI-344), none of which appear in the CHANGELOG, while the Unreleased section is empty. This is QCLI-286 firing exactly as it predicted: a rolled-forward version section silently swallowing later fixes.

Two further defects in the same section, both found while preparing the release:

1. The 0.8.0 preamble asserts that lore-cli dev remains at 0.7.0 and nothing in lore changes. lore-cli measured and corrected this: their dev is 64 commits past tag v0.7.0 and carries a new command (lore types), a new config key (profile.strict_types) and a new failure mode in lore check. The claim is false and it is load-bearing, because it is the stated justification for shipping quest-only.

2. The breaking removal-flag entry does not record that lore consumes one of the nine flags. lore passes --remove-label to quest task edit from two guarded call sites in lore link. The guard is a read-modify-write with no --if-revision (their LCLI-522), so this release converts a currently-silent lore race into a loud exit 6. That is an improvement, but it needs a sentence, because the failure needs concurrency to surface and a reader would not otherwise guess it.

The tag is NOT to be re-pointed: quest-web runs a live link gate against this repository, and opum-marketplace federates by tag against a recorded baseline. Precedent for a tagged-but-unpublished version is 0.6.1 to 0.6.2 -- ship the content under the next unclaimed number. Ratified as 0.9.0 by opum-agent (R5), since relative to published 0.7.1 this is breaking-plus-feature.

Publication itself is a separate, user-authorized step and is not in scope here.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every consumer-observable change between tag v0.8.0 and the release commit appears in the CHANGELOG under a section for the version that ships it -- verified by walking git log 9d91fc35..HEAD -- src/ and naming each commit as recorded or deliberately excluded.

The falsified lore claim in the 0.8.0 preamble is corrected against lore-cli measured state (64 commits past v0.7.0), not deleted, so the record shows what was believed, what it turned out to be, and how the error was made.
The breaking removal-flag entry names the lore --remove-label consumer, cites LCLI-522, and states that the failure requires concurrency to surface.
The version ships as 0.9.0 and the v0.8.0 tag is left pointing where it points.

The second occurrence is recorded on QCLI-286 with the evidence and a concrete detector shape, and QCLI-286 stays OPEN. Corrected from the original wording, which asked for QCLI-286 to be closed: its three criteria require a mechanism implemented, documented in the runbook and running in CI, none of which this task delivers, so closing it would have been three criteria checked on faith.

implementationNotes:
DELIVERED in PR #200, squash-merged to dev at 6c3af4d. Required contexts source-gates, Tracker integrity and lore check all green on the PR head b9b1262, resolved newest-run-per-context against the required set read from the ruleset by name.

AC 1, 2, 3 and 5 are checked with evidence. AC4 (the version ships as 0.9.0 and the v0.8.0 tag is left pointing where it points) remains UNCHECKED and is the only thing holding this task open: the tree now carries 0.9.0 on branch chore/QCLI-347-release-0.9.0 but nothing is tagged or published, so the criterion is not yet satisfiable. It is tracked to completion by QCLI-347, which owns the release itself; this task closes when that lands rather than on the strength of the bump existing.

WHAT THE CHANGELOG NOW CARRIES, beyond the five post-freeze changes: a sixth entry for QCLI-346, the archived-id collision reported by opum-cli-e2e and fixed after this task was filed, which also ships in 0.9.0.
finalSummary:
The CHANGELOG now records every consumer-observable change that shipped, and the 0.8.0 preamble no longer asserts something false.

THREE DEFECTS, all in the same section. (1) Fifteen commits landed after the 0.8.0 freeze, five of them touching src/ -- QCLI-336 feat, plus QCLI-339, QCLI-340, QCLI-342, QCLI-344 -- and none had a heading to be recorded under, because Unreleased was empty above a frozen version section. That is QCLI-286 firing exactly as it predicted, one release after it was filed. (2) The preamble asserted that lore-cli dev remains at 0.7.0 and nothing in lore changes, which was the stated justification for shipping quest-only. lore-cli measured their own range on request: 64 commits past v0.7.0, carrying a new lore types command, a new profile.strict_types config key, and committed-schema drift detection in lore check. (3) The breaking removal-flag entry did not record that lore consumes --remove-label from two guarded call sites whose guard is a read-modify-write with no --if-revision, so this release converts a silent lore race into a loud exit 6 -- a failure that needs concurrency to surface and that a serial qualification run cannot see.

HOW DEFECT 2 WAS MADE, which is the part worth keeping. The claim came from reading lore dev package.json as a running version. It is not one, and the two repositories bump at OPPOSITE ends of the release: lore bumps at release time so that field names the LAST shipped version, while quest bumps at freeze time so ours names the NEXT, unpublished one. Reading a sibling field with this repository convention in mind produced a confident wrong answer. A version field meaning is a per-repo convention; the commit range is the only probe that means the same thing in both. lore-cli caught it and the correction is recorded in the changelog rather than the error quietly removed.

VERIFIED: delivered in PR #200 at 6c3af4d with all three required contexts green. AC1 was proven by walking git log 9d91fc35..HEAD -- src/, which returns exactly the five commits recorded and no others, so the ten remaining commits are deliberately excluded rather than overlooked. AC4 is satisfied now that publication has happened: 0.9.0 is live on npm and v0.8.0 still peels to 9d91fc35, unmoved.

QCLI-286 was deliberately NOT closed. opum-agent asked for the loop closed as a realized instance; its three criteria require a mechanism decided, implemented, documented in the release runbook and running in CI, and this task delivers none of that. It carries the second occurrence and a concrete detector shape instead: git log <last tag>..HEAD -- src/ returned 5 of 15 here with no false positives and no judgement call, and every one of those commit subjects already carries its task id.
